segments.narration: Two countries fought hard to not own this land. Egypt says it is Sudan's. Sudan says it is Egypt's.
Bir Tawil is 2,060 square kilometres of bare desert on the Egypt-Sudan border, with no town and nobody living there.
In 1899 Britain drew a political border along the 22nd parallel. Three years later it drew a second line for tribal use.
Here is the trap. Each line hands one country Bir Tawil and the other the Hala'ib Triangle. Only one is worth having.
Hala'ib is ten times larger and reaches the Red Sea. So both claim Hala'ib, both reject Bir Tawil, and the desert stays nobody's.
